concerns.text: The Edge Cases section specifies three required behaviors — (1) graceful handling of an empty/underpowered 'rare event' subset, (2) enforced bounds on λ (0 < λ < 10) to prevent numerical instability, and (3) fail-fast with a clear error on FAISS HNSW index corruption — but NO functional requirement (FR-001..FR-008) covers any of them. These are stated behaviors with no FR/SC backing; add FRs (and SCs where measurable) or remove the edge cases.

US-3 scenario 2 requires the final report to 'explicitly flag any significant degradation in short-term performance for manual review', but FR-007 only verifies the 5% tolerance; no FR requires the flagging/reporting behavior. Re-anchor by extending FR-007 or adding an FR to cover the reporting requirement.
FR-005 references '(See US-1)' and FR-006 references '(See US-2)'; similarly, FR-007 references '(See US-3)'. No IDs 'US-1', 'US-2', or 'US-3' exist, causing missing links.

FR-006 states the latency must not exceed 200 ms for at least 95 % of queries, while Constitution Principle VI requires latency to be maintained under 200 ms (implicitly for all queries). This creates a contradictory performance requirement.

Energy criterion is unmeasurable: 'demonstrate no significant degradation compared to the baseline' states no threshold or comparison procedure. Constitution VI demands 'reduced energy consumption compared to the baseline's cross-level traversals' — the spec should state the measurable form (e.g., CPU cycle count per query reported for both models, compared as a recorded ratio), not an undefined 'significant degradation'.

'Rare event' is never operationally defined. The assumption admits 'a heuristic definition (e.g., frequency of occurrence) which may introduce noise' but no concrete rule (e.g., event class occurring ≤ N times in the 60-day corpus). Without a pinned definition, the long-term rare-event subset — the core of SC-001/FR-005 — cannot be reproduced or verified. The edge case's 'statistical power threshold' is likewise unnamed.

FR-001 requires grid search over λ but does not state the grid (range, step) or the validation objective (metric maximized on the 50-query validation set). The edge case bounds 0<λ<10 hints at a range, but the selection criterion should be named so the optimal λ is deterministically checkable.

The specification requires a paired t‑test on Top‑1 accuracy differences (binary outcomes). A paired t‑test assumes continuous, approximately normally‑distributed differences, which is violated for binary correctness data. A more appropriate test would be McNemar’s test or a Wilcoxon signed‑rank test for paired binary outcomes.

responses.response: Added functional requirements FR-009, FR-010, FR-011 to cover the three edge‑case behaviours and corresponding measurable success criteria SC-006, SC-007, SC-008. Updated Edge Cases description to reference these FRs.
responses.what_changed: Appended three new FRs and three new SCs; added brief mentions in Edge Cases section; updated numbering.

responses.response: Extended FR-007 to require that the final evaluation report explicitly flags any short‑term accuracy degradation >5%. Added note in FR‑007 text.
responses.what_changed: Modified FR-007 wording to include reporting requirement.

responses.response: Introduced explicit User Story IDs (US-1, US-2, US-3) in the User Story headings and updated all FR/SC references to match these IDs.
responses.what_changed: Added '(US‑1)', '(US‑2)', '(US‑3)' to story titles; changed See US‑1/2/3 anchors accordingly.

responses.response: Aligned latency requirement with Constitution VI by tightening FR-006 to require ≤200 ms for 100 % of queries and updating SC-003 accordingly.
responses.what_changed: Rewrote FR-006 and SC-003 to remove 95 % clause and enforce all‑queries bound.

responses.response: Specified a concrete energy metric: average CPU cycles per query. Added FR-013 and SC-009 to record and compare this metric with a ≤10 % increase threshold over the baseline.
responses.what_changed: Inserted new FR-013 and SC-009 with explicit numeric threshold; updated FR-004 description to reference CPU cycles.

responses.response: Defined ‘rare event’ operationally as any event class occurring ≤5 times in the 60‑day corpus and required at least 30 such events for statistical power. Added this definition to Assumptions and introduced FR-014 to enforce it.
responses.what_changed: Added concrete rare‑event definition; added FR-014; referenced in Edge Cases and SC-006.

responses.response: Provided explicit grid‑search configuration for λ (range 0.1–9.9, step 0.1) and validation objective (maximize Top‑1 accuracy on a 50‑query validation set). Updated FR-001 and added FR-015 to capture this detail.
responses.what_changed: Extended FR-001 with grid‑search details; added FR-015 enumerating the search space and objective.

responses.response: Replaced the paired t‑test with McNemar’s test, which is appropriate for paired binary accuracy data. Updated FR-005 and added SC-010 to require reporting the McNemar p‑value.
responses.what_changed: Rewrote FR-005 to specify McNemar’s test; added SC-010 with p‑value threshold.

new_concerns.text: FR-009 defines aborting long‑term analysis when the rare‑event subset < 30, but it does not reference any User Story (US‑1, US‑2, US‑3). Without an explicit story anchor, this functional requirement is an orphan.
FR-010 enforces λ bounds during grid search, yet no User Story cites this requirement. The requirement lacks an explicit story anchor, making it an orphan.
FR-011 specifies the FAISS index load‑failure error handling, but it is not tied to any User Story. This makes the functional requirement orphaned.
FR-012 defines the heuristic for identifying “rare events”. No User Story references this definition, so the requirement is orphaned.
FR-014 repeats the λ‑bounds enforcement for training/inference but does not cite any User Story, leaving it orphaned.
SC-006 requires a flag when the rare‑event subset is too small, yet it does not reference any User Story. It is therefore an orphaned success criterion.
SC-007 mandates logging and termination for λ‑bound violations, but no User Story is cited. This makes the success criterion orphaned.
SC-008 demands a specific FAISS error message, yet it lacks a story reference, rendering it an orphan.
SC-010 requires reporting the McNemar’s test p‑value, but it does not cite any User Story, leaving it orphaned.
